name: Захист від мату: перекриття
description:
Blocking or interposing as a means to defend is not new to you. You block an attack by moving a piece in between the attacker and the attacked piece. You can also use this technic to prevent mate. One of your pieces moves between the attacker and the mating square.

Study example 1.

Don’t be reckless when blocking. Make sure you move your piece to a safe spot.
Have a look at example 2. White has three different ways of blocking a mating attack. But only one of them is good.

What do you have to do?
Defend against checkmate by placing a piece between the attacker and the mating square. Make sure your piece is well protected.

examples.text:
Black’s queen wants to give checkmate on the green square.
The mating square is guarded by the black bishop.
But white is clever!
He pushes his pawn between the bishop and the mating square. Now, the black queen would be foolish to go there!

Black’s rook wants to give checkmate on the (green) square in the corner. This mating square is guarded by the black bishop.
But White is smart!
He remembers blocking as a means to defend.

There are three ways in which White can use his knight to block the attack.
It could follow one of the red arrows.
Good idea? No. It would make the knight a free capture for the black rook.
White would lose 3 points, with checkmate still hanging over him…

Then what? Watch the moves. Did you see?
White can move his knight between the bishop and the mating square.
There, it is defended by the king. Should the bishop take the knight, White simply regains it. An even trade and no checkmate for White!
